about: Non-contact and tip-free dispensers (#85). Engine fields chosen from data/dispensers-research.json (every figure there has a URL and quote, gathered 5 Nov 2026); content/dispensers.json is built from this file by scripts/build-dispensers.mjs, which adds each device's sources and price evidence from the research. suspensions: true = cells and beads, a list = only those material classes, null = no record (treated as cannot). deadVolumeUl is per reagent (channel, chip, reservoir, cassette or source well) as each source defines it. Open-source DIY dispensers stay leads in content/open-hardware.json.

throughput.about: Dispense time per plate (#173) from each device's 'throughput' record: maker or distributor figures as {wells, ul, seconds}, each record with its source URL and quote. A step's volume between two figures for its plate is interpolated (sourced); at or below the smallest figure that figure is used (sourced, an upper bound); a denser plate's figure stands in for a sparser plate (sourced, an upper bound). Beyond the largest figure the time is extrapolated from the last two figures, a 'starting from' figure is a best case, and a device with no figure uses the dispensing planning estimate in content/operations.json: all three are marked assumed. primeSeconds is null where no maker states a prime time; loading and priming are the person's dispenserLoad planning estimate.

comparisonDefault.why: The comparison opens on the best setup in scope on an OT-2 or Flex; choose another setup to compare there.

positive-displacement.label: Positive-displacement syringe
positive-displacement.how: A disposable syringe per reagent head draws from a reservoir and ejects drops without touching the well.

micro-diaphragm.label: Micro-diaphragm chip
micro-diaphragm.how: A reusable chip with valves and a diaphragm pumps fixed drops from a small reservoir; chips are washed between reagents.

solenoid.label: Solenoid valve
solenoid.how: A pressurised reagent line is opened by a fast valve; drop size set by pressure and opening time.

pressure-droplet.label: Pressure-driven droplet
pressure-droplet.how: Air pressure pushes drops through a hole in the base of each disposable source-plate well; no fluid path to clean.

acoustic.label: Acoustic droplet ejection
acoustic.how: Sound pulses eject nanolitre drops upward from a source-plate well into an inverted destination plate; no tips and no contact.

peristaltic.label: Peristaltic tubing
peristaltic.how: A pump drives liquid through a tubing cassette with 8 or more nozzles; bulk filling of whole plates.

reagentAccounting.about: Dead volume per addition step when the reagent is added by hand or by a liquid handler with tips; dispensers use their own figures above. A reagent prepared as a mix earlier in the workflow is made with an overage: the extra beyond what the wells receive is the larger of the container's dead volume and the overage (#119). A dispenser's prime volume is reported as volume to load, not counted as used.

column.label: Liquid-handler reservoir column or trough for heads of up to 16 channels: the low end is a maker figure for a 12-column robot reservoir (Porvair 391004, under 54 µL per column, from a distributor listing); the high end is assumed (no maker figure found for troughs read with liquid-level detection)

head.label: Single-well reservoir for a 96- or 384-channel head: Thermo's automation reservoirs need 5 mL (96-channel) and 4 mL (384-channel)

sourcePlate.label: Or a source plate with one well per channel: 15–20 µL extra per PCR-plate well (Agilent's aliquoting guidance for its 96-channel head); the smaller of reservoir and source plate is used

masterMix.label: Mix made with 10–25% overage (reagent makers' guidance for setting up by hand); on a liquid handler the reservoir dead volume usually sets the extra instead

sources.quote: Include an additional 10% of the master mix volume to account for variations in pipetting.
For every four reactions, include volume for a fifth reaction to provide excess volume
For multiple samples, multiply each volume by the number of samples plus 10% overage.
which equates to 23 % more master mix needed per 96 well plate compared to the microcentrifuge tube
